key_insight: A topological-conjugacy transform maps free-boundary PDEs to equivalent fixed-domain problems so neural operators can learn the solution operator reliably; applying the inverse transform reconstructs the evolving boundary and original-field solution.
problem_solved: Neural operators typically struggle with domains whose boundaries change in time (free-boundary problems like glacier melt). This framework enables accurate operator learning and prediction for such moving-boundary systems.
method: Construct a topological-conjugacy mapping that converts the free-boundary PDE into an equivalent fixed-domain formulation.
Train a neural operator on the transformed fixed-domain problem to learn the solution operator efficiently.
Apply the inverse conjugacy map to recover the original solution and the time-evolving boundary in the physical domain.
impact: Makes neural operators applicable to a broad class of real-world PDEs with moving boundaries (e.g., glaciology, multiphase flows), providing fast, generalizable surrogates for simulation, forecasting, and uncertainty quantification.
visual_elements: Schematic: free-boundary domain → conjugacy transform → fixed domain (side-by-side comparison)
Pipeline flowchart: data / PDE → transform → neural operator training → inverse transform → predicted solution + boundary
Animation or sequence: predicted glacier melt (boundary evolution) vs ground-truth simulation
Performance plots: error vs baseline solver and runtime / speedup bar chart
